strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP problem: assessing degrees of human contribution in collaborative text generation beyond binary AI-text detection. It appropriately acknowledges that informational contribution differs from creativity and legal authorship.

The empirical coverage is substantial: four domains, multiple generation and scoring models, repeated generations, and WildChat examples. The consistent ordering across prompting conditions supports the score’s usefulness as an ordinal signal in these settings.

The human study provides encouraging evidence on the selected comparisons: 1,500 pairs receive three independent annotations, with 91.47% unanimous agreement and 95.93% agreement between majority judgments and the input-aware measure.

The scoring procedure is simple and requires no additional model training. Appendix A documents dataset sources, prompt templates, model versions, and threshold values, providing useful methodological detail.
weaknesses: The central information-theoretic interpretation needs correction. Equation 5 computes a pointwise log-likelihood ratio, not Shannon mutual information. Interpreting it as pointwise mutual information additionally requires a compatible joint distribution; the unprompted model distribution is not shown to be the marginal over human inputs. The normalized score can also be negative when the input is known. These issues do not invalidate its use as a predictive score, but they undermine the interpretation as a nonnegative percentage of information attributable to humans.

Appendix B derives a lower bound conditional on an imposed plausibility threshold, then substitutes that bound for the minimum in Equation 10 without establishing attainability or tightness. Setting the conditional-surprisal threshold to an empirical mean plus one standard deviation provides no demonstrated coverage guarantee across domains or prompts. Held-out coverage and threshold-sensitivity analyses are needed to support claims about information necessarily supplied by humans. Moreover, a geometric-mean probability threshold does not prevent individual tokens from having extremely low probabilities, contrary to the stated rationale.

The output-only estimator is exactly a monotonic transformation of average text surprisal: with h = I(y)/N and c = -log(tau), Equation 10 becomes 1 - c/h. For a fixed scorer and threshold, it therefore produces the same rankings and ROC–AUC as average negative log-likelihood. The reported detection results cannot independently validate the minimum-contribution interpretation, and this equivalence should be explicitly acknowledged when positioning the contribution.

The validation is insufficiently independent of the proposed measure. Human-evaluation pairs are selected only when this measure already separates them by more than 0.1, so the high agreement rates do not establish performance on representative or closely matched examples. The synthetic conditions also strongly vary input length and textual overlap. Unfiltered, stratified human comparisons and baselines using length ratios, lexical or semantic overlap, and likelihood are needed. Current results establish broad ordering more convincingly than calibrated contribution percentages.

Several robustness claims exceed the tests performed. The two 'adaptive attacks' are fixed appended instructions without an optimization procedure or feedback from the score. Similarly, WildChat category differences provide coarse observational validation, while the multi-round experiments use generic model instructions without independently verified human corrections. These experiments support narrower claims than reliable attribution in realistic or adversarial co-writing workflows.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful appendix. The manuscript supplies no code or constructed-data access and leaves consequential likelihood-scoring details unspecified, including conditional versus unconditional chat formatting, scored token boundaries, and treatment of sampling temperature. Correcting the central interpretation and strengthening independent validation are necessary before a sound Findings recommendation; the current contribution warrants revision for the next cycle.
